title: Think first. Build clearly. Review before shipping.
intro: This is the part I care about most. I do not start with tools. I start with the problem, the edge cases, the data flow, and what might break later.

decisionGuide.label: I use AI for
items: Building first versions of components from clear specs
Comparing a few ways to build something

decisionGuide.label: I do myself
items: Reviewing every generated line before shipping

stages.label: 01 Understand
stages.title: Understand the real problem first
stages.summary: Before I build anything, I make the problem clear. What is actually broken? Who is affected? What matters most here?
details: I define the user, the failure point, and where the experience starts to break.
I separate the visible issue from the real cause.
I define what success looks like before I build.
stages.aiRole: AI can help me summarize notes, compare options, or draft a checklist.
stages.myRole: I decide what problem matters, what tradeoffs matter, and what done actually means.

stages.label: 02 Model
stages.title: Design the system before the UI
stages.summary: I think about data flow first. State, APIs, permissions, and error states come before polish.
details: I map where data starts, how it changes, and where it can get out of sync.
I plan for loading, empty, error, and partial-data states from the start.
I treat security as part of the build, not cleanup at the end.
signals: What is the source of truth?
Where can delay or inconsistency show up?
What should this user never be able to do?
stages.aiRole: AI helps me move faster on diagrams, endpoint drafts, schema drafts, and outlines.
stages.myRole: I review the structure, catch weak assumptions, and make sure it matches real product behavior.

stages.label: 03 Build
stages.title: Use AI for speed, not thinking
stages.summary: Once the behavior is clear, I use AI to move faster. But only after the constraints, states, and contracts are already defined.
details: I write prompts from specs, not guesses.
I use AI for first drafts, repetitive work, refactors, and alternatives.
I keep the work grounded in clear expectations so the code stays easy to review.
signals: Can I explain every line this tool generated?
Did the code keep the edge cases right?
Would I still ship this if my name alone were on it?
stages.aiRole: AI speeds up implementation, repetition, and trying a few options quickly.
stages.myRole: I own correctness, clarity, security, and whether the final code should ship.

stages.label: 04 Review
stages.title: Review everything like a PR
stages.summary: Generated or not, I review code carefully. I verify behavior, question assumptions, and test the parts most likely to fail.
details: I look for brittle logic, missing states, and shortcuts that only work in ideal cases.
I test edge cases, bad data paths, and permission boundaries.
I clean up naming, structure, and UX until the work feels solid.
signals: If this breaks, where does it break first?
What did the happy path hide?
Is the product clearer now than it was before?
stages.aiRole: AI can suggest tests, point out risky branches, or give a second pass on refactors.
stages.myRole: I make the final shipping call. If I cannot explain it, it does not go live.
